newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weaker after yen surge.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weaker after yen surge.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished weaker on Monday in line with the underlying cash market due to pressure from a stronger yen, dealers said.
The yen's surge against the dollar was seen hurting Japanese exports and the perception triggered sales in export-linked stocks in the Tokyo stock market, they said.
Dealers said unwinding of positions in the nearby expiring June futures contract added to overall weakness.
"The market is bearish but held support. Liquidation was mostly in the Junes because of switchover trades," a dealer with a European commission house said.
The June Nikkei was down 225 points at 20,300 after climbing to an intraday high of 20,580. September also fell the same amount to 20,340. A total of 22,673 contracts traded.
The Nikkei index opened up following Wall Street's strong close on Friday, but the yen's surge later turned sentiment.

Dollar/yen traded to a low of 111.80 on renewed concerns about Japan's trade surplus. Dealers expect Nikkei futures to hold at 20,200 support unless dollar/yen slides past 111.80, which could then lead the Nikkei past 20,000 support, they said.
